presets.label: gpu1 — RTX 4090, 24 GB (remote)
presets.note: The fastest lane in the fleet: 18.20 fps sustained, full-frame, no window. gpu1 holds a copy of the archive, so each clip is read in place and stage_source stays off.

presets.label: encoder-host — Radeon 8060S iGPU (local)
presets.note: 128 GB of unified memory holds the full-frame state, so this lane needs no tiling and no window. 4.08 fps over three full-clip runs, and 2.37 fps while this host also encodes. It uses its own interpreter, because the MIGraphX wheels stop at cp312.

presets.label: encoder-host — RTX 2070 SUPER, 8 GB (local)
presets.note: 8 GB cannot hold the 7.4 GB full-frame state, so this card must run tiled and windowed. Window 750 measured 4.7% faster end to end than 500, for 40.6 GB of host RAM against 29.1 GB. device is 0, not 1: CUDA enumerates only the NVIDIA card.

presets.label: gpu2 — RTX 5070 Laptop (remote)
presets.note: 4.07 fps on driver 610.88, GPU-bound at 92.8%, with no fault in eight runs. Window 750 completed 0 of 8 attempts on this card, so keep 300. gpu2 holds no archive, so every clip is copied to it and its Temp/_remote grows all run.

presets.label: gpu4 — GB10 (remote)
presets.note: Full-frame and unwindowed: 4.37 fps sustained after 12.1 s of overhead. The checkout on this host is ubuntav1an, not archav1an. gpu4 holds no archive, so every clip is copied to it.

presets.label: gpu5 — GB10 (remote)
presets.note: gpu4's twin: the same GB10, 20 cores and 121 GB, so it takes the same settings — full-frame, no window, 4.37 fps sustained. No archive of its own, so every clip is copied to it.

presets.label: gpu3 — RTX 3070 Laptop, 8 GB (remote)
presets.note: About 4.89 fps end to end at window 500. Window 750 is 3% faster but takes 39.3 GB of this host's 47 GB. The card throttles to 1292 MHz under load, and to about half the rate on Thunderbolt power.
